book_title: Asas al-Taweel — Volume 1: The Cycle of Adam

chapters.title: What Ismaili Interpretation Is
chapters.theme: the nature and validity of ta'wil — the inward dimension of revelation
chapters.rationale: Establishes the hermeneutic premise: outward and inward meaning are both obligatory; al-Nu'man grounds this in Quran, hadith, and the logic of divine speech before opening the Adam cycle.

chapters.title: The Call to Inner Meaning
chapters.theme: the obligatory inward call (da'wa) that accompanies every outward revelation
chapters.rationale: Al-Nu'man shifts from theory to proof — every prophet carried both a public teaching and a hidden invitation to those who could receive it; the Imam inherits this dual function.

chapters.title: The Four Limits of the Testimony
chapters.theme: the shahada parsed into four stations: limits, gates, sincerity, and the rank of the Imam
chapters.rationale: The testimony of faith is not a formula but a cosmological map — each clause assigns the believer a position in the hierarchy of guidance, from outer acknowledgment to inner loyalty.

chapters.title: Adam, the Tree, and the Iblis Pact
chapters.theme: the Adam narrative read as the origin of the two parties — guided and misguided — in every age
chapters.rationale: Al-Nu'man opens the Adam cycle not as history but as a living pattern: the tree, the pact, and Iblis's refusal are the templates for every subsequent cycle of the natiq and his opponents.

chapters.title: Two Parties and the Line to Noah
chapters.theme: the covenant-keeping party traced from Adam through Seth to Noah; the opposing party tracing through Iblis
chapters.rationale: The Adam cycle closes by showing that the two parties do not dissolve with Adam's death — they persist through named genealogies, binding every subsequent natiq to the same primordial division.
